title: Binary decoding assertion accepts every possible return value
reasoning: The assertion result is not None or result is None is always true. The test therefore provides no check on decoding behavior, despite its stated expectation. Its comments also acknowledge a Latin-1 fallback, so the excerpt does not establish that returning decoded text is itself a production bug.
reproduction: Return any arbitrary value for this input; the assertion still passes.
recommendation: Replace the tautology with an explicit expectation derived from the intended decoding contract and align the test name with that contract.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The other decoding tests cover ordinary UTF-8 and Latin-1 strings, while the binary snapshot test checks exclusion from text diffs rather than this helper's return behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Expand the existing decoding scenarios to assert the defined outcome for non-UTF-8 input containing control bytes, including the exact decoded text if Latin-1 fallback is intended.
